title: Guard yourself from the Fire prepared for the disbelievers.
subtitle: A warning placed right after the loan verse

row.title: guard yourself
sub: in how you deal and earn

row.title: dealings matter
sub: warned of in the same breath

then: Ibn Kathir notes that after forbidding multiplied interest, Allah {trap}warns them against the Fire{/trap} and commands them to {idea}obey Allah and the Messenger that they may obtain mercy{/idea}. The warning sits right beside a money matter.
now: You think of the Hereafter in the mosque, not at the checkout, not in the contract, not in the loan you're about to sign. {idea}The Quran puts them in the same paragraph.{/idea}
old: How I handle money is separate from my faith.
new: My dealings with money are part of what protects me from the Fire, or exposes me to it.
try: Before your next financial decision, pause and ask if Allah would be pleased with it.

title: Obey Allah and the Messenger, that you may receive mercy.
subtitle: Obedience as the path to mercy
then: After the warning comes the way out. Ibn Kathir pairs this verse with the previous one: {trap}fear the Fire{/trap}, and {reward}obey Allah and the Messenger that you may obtain mercy{/reward}.
now: Your alarm for Fajr goes off and obedience feels like a cost. Then you stand in the quiet and something settles. {reward}That calm is mercy coming through the door you opened.{/reward}
old: Obeying is something I do for Allah, and it costs me.
new: Obeying is how I place myself where His mercy falls.
try: Do one act of obedience today you've been delaying, and notice how you feel afterward.

title: Hurry to forgiveness and a Garden as wide as heavens and earth.
subtitle: Hurry, there is room

row.title: life is short
sub: the room is endless, the time is not

then: Ibn Kathir notes Allah {idea}encourages rushing to good deeds{/idea}, and the width points to Paradise's vastness. He cites the Prophet ﷺ: when you ask for Paradise, {reward}ask for al-Firdaws, the highest{/reward}.
now: You hurry for a sale that ends at midnight, the last train, a concert ticket drop. {idea}Bring that urgency here.{/idea} The Garden is wide; your days are not.
old: There's always time to get serious about Paradise later.
new: Paradise has endless room, but my time to hurry toward it is limited.
try: When you make dua today, ask Allah for al-Firdaws by name.

title: They give in ease and hardship, swallow anger, and pardon.
subtitle: Three marks of the people of the Garden

row.title: they hold anger
sub: though able to act on it

then: Ibn Kathir cites the Prophet ﷺ: {reward}the strong one is he who controls himself when angry{/reward}. And {idea}no gulp is dearer to Allah than a gulp of anger a servant swallows{/idea}, which fills him with faith.
now: Someone cuts you off in traffic. Your teenager slams the door. Your boss blames you in front of everyone. {idea}The gulp is right there.{/idea} Swallow it, then let it go.
old: If I don't react, people will walk all over me.
new: Holding back anger and pardoning is strength Allah loves, not weakness.
try: The next time anger rises today, wait ten seconds before answering, and forgive one small thing.

title: When they slip, they remember Allah and ask forgiveness.
subtitle: The people of the Garden also sin
then: Ibn Kathir cites the hadith: a man sins and says {idea}Lord, I sinned, forgive me{/idea}, and Allah says {reward}My servant knew he has a Lord who forgives; I have forgiven him{/reward}. It repeats again and again. Anas was told that when this verse came, Iblis wept.
now: Same sin, third time this month. The voice says: stop pretending, you're a hypocrite. {reward}That voice is not Allah's.{/reward} {idea}Remember Him, ask again, and stop where you can.{/idea}
old: If I keep falling into the same sin, my repentance is fake.
new: Every return counts. The people of the Garden are those who keep coming back without persisting.
try: After your next slip, immediately say astaghfirullah and do one good deed to follow it.

title: Their reward: forgiveness and Gardens. What a reward for workers.
subtitle: Effort that is paid in full
then: This sums up the qualities of the last three verses: giving in all conditions, swallowing anger, pardoning, and returning after sin. Ibn Kathir: {reward}forgiveness and Gardens, forever{/reward}, and {idea}Allah praises this reward{/idea}.
now: Your payslip lists hours worked. This verse calls you a worker too. {idea}Every swallowed word, every pardon, every return after a fall, is logged.{/idea} {reward}And the pay is excellent.{/reward}
new: Paradise is the wage of those who keep working at goodness and keep returning.
try: Pick one of the qualities from verses 134 and 135 and practice it once today.

title: Others before you went through this. Look how it ended.
subtitle: Comfort after the losses at Uhud

row.title: only me
sub: no one ever had it this bad

row.title: a known pattern
sub: others passed through and the end was good

then: After Uhud, where {trap}seventy believers were killed{/trap}, Allah comforts them. Ibn Kathir: earlier nations who followed their prophets also suffered losses, yet {reward}the good end was theirs{/reward}. Travel and see.
now: The diagnosis, the layoff, the miscarriage. You feel like the first person ever to stand in this place. {idea}Others walked here before you, held on to faith, and came through.{/idea}
old: No one has ever gone through something like this.
new: Believers before me faced losses like mine, and the good end was theirs.
try: Read or listen to the story of one person, past or present, who kept faith through a loss like yours.

title: This is a clear statement, guidance, and a lesson.
subtitle: What the Quran does after a loss
then: Right after pointing to history, Allah says the Quran itself is {idea}a clear statement for mankind{/idea}. Ibn Kathir explains it shows the true reality of things and gives {reward}guidance for hearts and instruction{/reward} to keep away from what is forbidden.
now: After a hard week you open six tabs looking for an explanation. A podcast, a thread, an article. {idea}The clearest explanation is already on your shelf.{/idea}
old: I need someone to explain why this happened to me.
new: Allah has already given a clear statement that explains, guides, and instructs.
try: When something hard happens this week, read a few verses before reading anything else.

title: Do not weaken, do not grieve. You are higher, if you believe.
subtitle: Standing up again after defeat
then: The believers had just suffered heavy loss. Ibn Kathir: Allah comforts them, {idea}do not become weak because of what you suffered{/idea}, nor grieve, for {reward}the ultimate victory will be yours, O believers{/reward}.
now: You didn't get the promotion. The business failed. Your child is struggling and you feel like you failed them. {idea}Today's score is not your rank.{/idea} {reward}Faith keeps you higher.{/reward}
old: A defeat means I am beneath others now.
new: My rank comes from faith, not from today's result. I don't have to collapse.
try: After your next setback, stand up, make wudu, and pray two rak'ahs before deciding anything.

title: These days We rotate among people.
subtitle: Good days and hard days take turns

row.title: their wound
sub: the other side was hurt too

then: Ibn Kathir explains: if you were wounded, {trap}your enemies were also wounded{/trap}. The days take turns, out of wisdom, so Allah may show who is patient. Hardship {reward}forgives the believers' sins or raises their ranks{/reward}.
now: Last year everything went your way. This year, the car, the job, your health. {idea}Days rotate. That's not abandonment.{/idea} The hard turn is where patience gets seen.
old: When things go badly, it means Allah has turned against me.
new: Days rotate by His wisdom. Hard days reveal patience and are not wasted.
try: Write down one hard thing you are going through and next to it one way it might be refining you.
